result_kind: simulated (behavioural model B with T-extracted corner parameters; only the model's seed parameter was varied)
method_basis: issue #311; the DR-001 item 3 span_10pct leg (sim/bmodel/xcheck.py SPAN_REL_LIMIT)
which_side: B-side behavioural model (model.modulate_with_states); no transistor-level simulation is involved anywhere in this record
what_varied: only model parameter 'seed', over the seed list below; every other parameter is exactly the corner file's value and the input sequence is the committed T record's u_diff_v, unmodified
window: Blackman-Harris 4-term (the cross-check's spectral window, named per the record contract; span, percentile span, RMS and duty are time-domain statistics and do not apply it)

statistics.ptp_x*_fs: peak-to-peak of the integrator state, max - min: the gated statistic, verbatim as xcheck.py waveform_stats computes it
statistics.p1p99_x*_fs: 1st/99th-percentile span of the integrator state (numpy.percentile linear interpolation): alternative statistic, robust to the extreme order statistic
statistics.rms_x*_fs: sqrt(mean(x^2)) of the integrator state: alternative variance-like statistic
statistics.duty: mean of the +/-1 bitstream: the duty_0p05 leg's statistic
statistics.spread: (max - min) / midrange, midrange = (max + min) / 2, over the seed draw -- the definition behind issue #311's tt figures (o1 5.77 %, o2 13.39 % on the long input)

gates_quoted_not_changed.span_10pct: xcheck.py SPAN_REL_LIMIT = 0.10, quoted, not modified; changing the gated statistic or the limit is a DR-001 decision record (issue #311 out of scope)
gates_quoted_not_changed.duty_0p05: xcheck.py DUTY_LIMIT = 0.05 (absolute); the duty leg's seed spread is recorded beside it for comparison

long_record_leg.why: swept from sim/bmodel/xcheck-sides-long/ with the identical driver, seeds and statistics

committed-1024-clock.hypothesis: a peak-to-peak statistic is dominated by the extreme order statistic of the seeded noise, so its realisation spread falls far more slowly with record length than a variance-like statistic's (issue #311, unverified hypothesis)
committed-1024-clock.finding: the RMS is strictly tighter than the peak-to-peak at every anchor and both integrators, consistent with the extreme-order-statistic hypothesis for a variance-like statistic; the 1st/99th-percentile span is NOT uniformly tighter -- at these record lengths its tails still rest on ~1 % of the window, so it inherits part of the same exposure. The gated statistic is NOT changed here; if this evidence motivates a different one, that is a DR-001 decision record (issue #311 out of scope).

long-record.hypothesis: a peak-to-peak statistic is dominated by the extreme order statistic of the seeded noise, so its realisation spread falls far more slowly with record length than a variance-like statistic's (issue #311, unverified hypothesis)
long-record.finding: at every anchor and both integrators both alternative statistics have strictly smaller seed spread than the peak-to-peak: consistent with the extreme-order-statistic hypothesis. The gated statistic is NOT changed here; if this evidence motivates a different one, that is a DR-001 decision record (issue #311 out of scope).

record_len_note: per DR-001 item 5: record length (per anchor, under input_sets[].n_clocks), window, bin bandwidth and the producing side are named on every number; every number here is simulated, nothing measured
